title: A Bell for the Room
premise: Felix Almeida, a pest controller with a decade of rationalizations behind them, takes one last job at the Harrow house, where something leaves fingerprints on the inside of sealed walls. The house's mirrors lag a second behind reality, and in that stolen second Felix glimpses the children who vanished there generations ago—children who survived by learning a song that keeps the thing in the well fed. As the well refills and the song's final verse surfaces through the plumbing, Felix must decide whether to sing along and inherit the house's covenant of complicity, or finish the verse alone and break it. In the end, Felix sings the last verse as an accusation rather than a lullaby; the well drains for good, but the fingerprints remain on Felix's own hands, a price they carry out the door.
about_author: A. M. Vasquez is a former building inspector who spent years cataloguing the strange things people leave inside their walls before turning to fiction. They write horror about houses that remember, and live quietly in a home with no mirrors in the hallway.

chapters.title: The Call Sheet
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Felix, who accepts the Harrow job against their better judgment because rent is due. The emotional beat is weary pragmatism masking dread.

chapters.title: Something With Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Felix inspects the basement and finds small handprints pressed into fresh mortar behind a sealed wall. POV stays with Felix; the beat is professional denial cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter to Felix's first haunting-adjacent call, establishing the rationalizations they've built. Third person; the beat is self-deception as survival skill.

chapters.title: The House That Waits
chapters.summary: Felix works late and hears footsteps above them in an empty second floor. The beat is the moment denial stops being comfortable.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Felix notices the hallway mirror reflecting their movements a full second behind. POV Felix; the beat is vertigo—the rules of reality shifting underfoot.

chapters.title: The Previous Owner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inherited from the estate: a ledger of payments, dates, and a column labeled 'verse.' Felix realizes the house was maintained like an obligation. Beat: inheritance as trap.

chapters.title: Neighbors Who Look Away
chapters.summary: Felix canvasses the street; neighbors are polite, evasive, and all glance at the well cover in the yard. Beat: a community complicit in silence.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix lowers a camera into the dry well and retrieves footage of small hands passing something upward. Beat: horror confirmed, no exit offered.

chapters.title: The First Verse
chapters.summary: A melody arrives through the pipes at 3 a.m.; Felix transcribes it compulsively. Beat: seduction—the song wants to be learned.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Introduce Mara Osei, an archivist whose great-aunt disappeared at the Harrow house in 1961. Dual purpose ally and warning. Beat: cautious alliance.

chapters.title: The Children in the Glass
chapters.summary: The lagging mirror shows three children standing where Felix stood a second ago. Beat: the dead aren't hostile—they're instructing.

chapters.title: Survival Has a Chorus
chapters.summary: Mara decodes the ledger: each generation sang to stay alive, and the singing fed the thing below. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Felix's Own Wall
chapters.summary: Flashback to the brother Felix lost and never reported missing properly; guilt rhymes with the house's covenant. Beat: why Felix understands complicity.

chapters.title: Second Verse, Second Voice
chapters.summary: The song gains harmony—something else is singing back through the drain. Beat: intimacy turned threat.

chapters.title: The Refill Begins
chapters.summary: Water rises in the dry well overnight, warm and smelling of iron. Beat: countdown established.

chapters.title: Do Not Sing Along
chapters.summary: Felix catches themselves humming and slams the piano lid on their own hands metaphorically. Beat: the enemy is internal now.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Box
chapters.summary: Mara finds her great-aunt's letters describing the last verse—and a warning that it was cut in half deliberately. Beat: hope with a splinter in it.

chapters.title: The Missing Half
chapters.summary: The verse's ending was torn from every record by whoever benefited most. Beat: justice outside the law begins to take shape.

chapters.title: Who Profits From Silence
chapters.summary: Felix traces the estate to a living descendant, Aldous Harrow, who sends a lawyer instead of answers. Beat: institutional rot.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Visit
chapters.summary: A sleek attorney offers Felix money to leave and sign an NDA. Felix refuses. Beat: temptation declined, stakes raised.

chapters.title: Night of the Open Doors
chapters.summary: Every interior door in the house stands open at once, and the mirror-lag stretches to five seconds. Beat: the house losing patience.

chapters.title: What the Children Want
chapters.summary: Through the glass, the eldest child mouths two words: last verse. Beat: the dead recruit the living.

chapters.title: Mara's Doubt
chapters.summary: Mara admits part of her wants the song completed so she can hear her aunt's voice again. Beat: grief as vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Well at Half
chapters.summary: Half full. The water shows reflections of its own, independent of light. Beat: dread deepening toward inevitability.

chapters.title: Aldous Harrow Comes Home
chapters.summary: The descendant arrives in person, old and unafraid, and reveals he sang here as a boy. Beat: the villain is also a survivor.

chapters.title: The Covenant Explained
chapters.summary: Aldous lays it out plainly: sing, inherit, live; refuse, and be taken. He offers Felix his place someday. Beat: the devil's arithmetic.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Felix refuses—not heroically, but out of a stubborn refusal to become another name in the ledger. Beat: quiet defiance.

chapters.title: The House Turns
chapters.summary: Locked in overnight, Felix survives by staying silent while the song tries every register to draw them in. Beat: endurance as resistance.

chapters.title: The Child Who Wouldn't Sing
chapters.summary: The mirror reveals a fourth child—one who refused in 1931 and paid for it. Her story becomes the map. Beat: precedent for rebellion.

chapters.title: Reconstructing the Last Verse
chapters.summary: Felix and Mara assemble the torn half from the fourth child's scratched wall-writing. Beat: collaborative hope.

chapters.title: It Isn't a Lullaby
chapters.summary: They realize the final verse isn't a feeding song—it's an accusation, meant to be sung at the well, not to it. Beat: revelation reframing everything.

chapters.title: Aldous Interferes
chapters.summary: Aldous steals the transcription to protect his inheritance, forcing a confrontation in the flooding cellar. Beat: betrayal at the worst hour.

chapters.title: The Well at Full
chapters.summary: The well brims. The house goes utterly silent, which is worse than the song. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Singing Alone
chapters.summary: Felix descends and sings the last verse solo, voice shaking, refusing the harmonies offered from below. Beat: climax—courage without company.

chapters.title: The Accusation Lands
chapters.summary: The water convulses; the fingerprints appear on the surface like a confession, then sink. The well begins to drain. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: What It Costs
chapters.summary: The draining pulls at Felix; Mara hauls them out, but the handprints have transferred to Felix's palms. Beat: victory with a scar.

chapters.title: Aldous's End
chapters.summary: Aldous, hearing his covenant void, walks into the empty well of his own accord—or is taken; the house doesn't explain. Beat: grim justice.

chapters.title: Empty Mirrors
chapters.summary: The mirrors reflect in real time now, showing only ordinary rooms. The children are gone—freed or spent, unknowable. Beat: ambiguous peace.

chapters.title: The Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Felix burns the ledger, keeps one page as evidence, and gives testimony Mara will archive publicly. Beat: justice outside the law, on the record.

chapters.title: Hands That Remember
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Felix returns to work, gloves over marked hands, telling new clients the noises have explanations—but keeping the song's last verse memorized, just in case. Beat: survival, changed forever.
